findings.title: Over-committed minimum: 75.0% of a $480,000/yr floor used
findings.summary: AtlasCloud (IaaS) carries a $480,000/yr committed minimum but consumed only $360,000 (75.0% utilization) — a $120,000 take-or-pay shortfall paid for and not used. In-term the floor is owed; right-sizing the next-term commitment to $396,000 (consumption + 10% buffer) recaptures $84,000/yr. Raise this before the renewal notice deadline (2027-11-01, 492 days out).
findings.leverage: A documented multi-period utilization trend is the lever to lower the next-term minimum or convert take-or-pay to a drawdown/rollover. Over-commitment also signals the original deal was oversold — leverage for additional concessions. Tie to R01 timing: present before the notice deadline.

evidence.value: minCommitSpend $480,000 / annual

evidence.label: Actual consumption (12 invoices)
evidence.value: $360,000 (75.0% of the floor)

evidence.label: Right-sized commitment (consumption + buffer)
evidence.value: $396,000 (consumption + 10% buffer)

findings.recommendedAsk: Reduce the committed annual minimum from $480,000 to $396,000 at renewal (consumption of $360,000 + 10% buffer), or convert the take-or-pay floor to a drawdown/rollover so unused commit carries forward — a $84,000/yr right-sizing.

findings.title: Catalyst Creative Agency: 25 hour/monthly over allowance billed at punitive overage
findings.summary: Plan includes 40 hour/monthly, but invoices bill 65 (25 over) at $185.00/hour = $4,625/monthly ($55,500/yr) in overage. No higher-allowance tier is published; the entire $4,625/monthly in punitive overage is avoidable by buying up the base allowance from 40 to 65 units. Annualized avoidable savings $55,500.
findings.leverage: Consistent allowance breach means a higher base allowance (cheaper per unit) or a renegotiated overage rate beats paying punitive overage month after month.

evidence.label: Contract overage rate
evidence.value: $185.00 per hour

evidence.label: Billed usage (invoice)
evidence.value: 65 hour (25 over the 40 allowance)

findings.recommendedAsk: Buy up the base allowance from 40 to at least 65 hour/monthly, eliminating the $4,625/monthly punitive overage — $4,625/monthly ($55,500/yr).

findings.title: 90 idle seats of 250 paid (64.0% utilization)
findings.summary: Utilization export shows only 160 of 250 paid seats active within the 30-day activity window — 90 seats are billed but idle. Reclaiming them at renewal avoids $48,600/yr.
findings.leverage: Hard utilization data ('only N of M seats active') is the strongest right-sizing lever at renewal. Anchor on active seats, not provisioned. Offer to hold the per-seat rate flat plus a true-up clause to add seats later at the same price — it protects the vendor's unit economics and makes 'yes' easy. Pair with R01 timing so the ask lands before the notice deadline.

findings.recommendedAsk: Reduce the seat count from 250 to 160 active seats at renewal (drop 90 idle seats), holding the $45.00/seat/mo rate flat — an annual avoidance of $48,600.

findings.title: Auto-renewal notice window closing — act before July 12, 2026
findings.summary: PayWorks HCM auto-renews on August 11, 2026 (45 days out) at a 18.0% uplift, taking the contract from $190,800/yr to $225,144/yr. Written cancellation notice is due by July 12, 2026 (15 days away). Acting before that deadline opens a competitive renewal: the $34,344/yr uplift is negotiable and a price hold / escalator cap can be demanded as the condition of staying.
findings.leverage: An open (or contestable) notice window is the highest-leverage moment in the relationship: it converts an automatic renewal into a competitive event, forcing a price hold, escalator cap, and seat/commit right-sizing as the price of staying.

evidence.label: Term end date
evidence.value: August 11, 2026 (45 days from analysis date June 27, 2026)

evidence.label: Notice deadline
evidence.value: July 12, 2026 — 15 days away

evidence.label: Renewal uplift
evidence.value: 18.0% fixed escalator → renewal value $225,144/yr; negotiable uplift $34,344/yr

evidence.label: Early-termination fee
evidence.value: $45,000 termination fee deepens the lock-in

findings.recommendedAsk: Before the July 12, 2026 notice deadline, demand a price hold or convert to month-to-month and cap the renewal uplift — eliminating the 18.0% ($34,344/yr) increase on the $190,800/yr base.

findings.title: Above-market renewal: 22.0% uplift on CGL + Property Package Premium (monthly installment)PKG-CGL-PROP

findings.leverage: A compliant-but-above-market uplift is the renewal ask: convert it to a hard cap ('lesser of CPI or 5%'), traded for a multi-year commitment. A vendor's refusal to cap signals its pricing trajectory.

drafts.subject: AtlasCloud (IaaS) – right-sizing to actual usage
drafts.body:
Hi AtlasCloud (IaaS) team,

Ahead of our renewal we pulled utilization and consumption data. AtlasCloud (IaaS) carries a $480,000/yr committed minimum but consumed only $360,000 (75.0% utilization) — a $120,000 take-or-pay shortfall paid for and not used. In-term the floor is owed; right-sizing the next-term commitment to $396,000 (consumption + 10% buffer) recaptures $84,000/yr. Raise this before the renewal notice deadline (2027-11-01, 492 days out).

What we're seeing:
  • Committed annual minimum (take-or-pay floor): $480,000
  • Commitment terms (annual measurement period): minCommitSpend $480,000 / annual
  • Actual consumption (12 invoices): $360,000 (75.0% of the floor)
  • Monthly run-rate / range: $30,000/mo (low $30,000, high $30,000)

For renewal we'd like to Reduce the committed annual minimum from $480,000 to $396,000 at renewal (consumption of $360,000 + 10% buffer), or convert the take-or-pay floor to a drawdown/rollover so unused commit carries forward — a $84,000/yr right-sizing.. To keep this simple and protect your unit economics, we'll hold the per-unit rate flat and add a true-up provision so we can scale back up at the same price. A documented multi-period utilization trend is the lever to lower the next-term minimum or convert take-or-pay to a drawdown/rollover. Over-commitment also signals the original deal was oversold — leverage for additional concessions. Tie to R01 timing: present before the notice deadline.

Can you have a revised order form to us by November 1, 2027? We'd rather expand from a clean baseline than carry shelfware into another term.

Best regards,
Jordan Avery
VP, Finance, Northwind Logistics Group, Inc.
jordan.avery@northwindlogistics.com

drafts.subject: Keystone Mutual Insurance renewal pricing – capping the annual uplift
drafts.body:
Hi Keystone Mutual Insurance team,

Thanks for the renewal terms. The applied increase is out of line with both our agreement and the market. Keystone Mutual Insurance raised "CGL + Property Package Premium (monthly installment)PKG-CGL-PROP" 22.0% year-over-year ($10,000.00 -> $12,200.00/mo), far above the 8.0% above-market threshold and the fair 3-5% band (CPI 3.2%). With no contractual cap, the full $26,400/yr uplift is challengeable at renewal — convert it to a hard cap.

What we're seeing:
  • Contract escalator clause: Escalator type "fixed", no cap; market fair band is 3-5% (CPI 3.2%)
  • Prior-period rate (May 2025): CGL + Property Package Premium (monthly installment)PKG-CGL-PROP: $10,000.00/mo (= $120,000/yr base)
  • Escalated rate (Jun 2026): CGL + Property Package Premium (monthly installment)PKG-CGL-PROP: $12,200.00/mo (+22.0% year-over-year)
  • Benchmark applied: Above-market threshold 8.0% — applied 22.0% (CPI 3.2%, BLS CPI-U trailing 12mo (May 2026): 3.2%)

Here's a structure that works for both sides: Cap the renewal increase at "lesser of CPI or 5%" and roll the 22.0% uplift back toward fair market, recovering $26,400/yr of above-market spend. — a contractual cap on any future increase (the lesser of CPI or 3–5%). In exchange we're prepared to commit to a multi-year term, which gives you revenue visibility. A compliant-but-above-market uplift is the renewal ask: convert it to a hard cap ('lesser of CPI or 5%'), traded for a multi-year commitment. A vendor's refusal to cap signals its pricing trajectory.
